title: Loihi
intro: Loihi is Intel's line of research neuromorphic processors. The first chip, announced in 2017 and described by Davies et al. in 2018, ran spiking networks entirely on-chip with programmable synaptic plasticity. Loihi 2 (2021) added programmable neuron models and graded spikes. The chips are available to researchers through Intel's Neuromorphic Research Community and are programmed with the open-source Lava framework.

items: Process and scale: a 14 nm chip with 128 neuromorphic cores and 3 embedded x86 cores for management, supporting up to about 130,000 neurons and 130 million synapses.

Neurons: each core implements up to 1024 compartments of a current-based leaky integrate-and-fire model (CUBA LIF), with separate synaptic-current and membrane decays. Compartments can be combined into multi-compartment neurons with dendritic trees.

Communication: an asynchronous mesh network-on-chip carries spike messages between cores (address-event style). Time advances in algorithmic time steps that cores agree on through a barrier handshake, so the chip runs as fast as activity allows, not on a fixed real-time clock.
Memory: synaptic weights, delays and neuron states are stored in each core's SRAM. This is colocated memory and compute, and it is also the limit on network size per chip.
Scaling: chips tile into larger systems. Nahuku boards hold 32 chips, and Pohoiki Springs (2020) combined 768 chips for about 100 million neurons.

blocks.text: Loihi's signature feature is on-chip learning. Each core can update synaptic weights, delays and tags while the network runs, with rules written in a sum-of-products form over local variables:

blocks.source:
dw = sum_i  S_i * prod_j (V_ij + C_ij)

V_ij: local variables such as presynaptic traces x1, x2, postsynaptic traces y1, y2, y3,
      the current weight w, and a modulatory "reward" trace
C_ij: constants;   S_i: scaling factors

blocks.text: Because traces are available on both sides of each synapse, this covers pair-based STDP, triplet STDP, weight-dependent rules and three-factor rules in which a reward or error signal arrives through a special input. Learning epochs can run every few time steps to save energy. Demonstrations include online learning of odor representations in a model of the olfactory bulb (Imam & Cleland 2020) and few-shot gesture learning.

items: Built on a pre-production Intel 4 process, with up to about 1 million neurons per chip in a smaller die.
Programmable neurons: neuron models are microcode programs, so models beyond LIF (resonate-and-fire, adaptive neurons, custom dynamics) run natively.
Graded spikes: a spike can carry an integer payload instead of a single bit, which reduces message counts for rate-like signals.
Faster chip-to-chip links and support for 3-factor learning carried over and extended.
Hala Point (2024) combines 1152 Loihi 2 chips for about 1.15 billion neurons, the largest neuromorphic system reported at the time.

blocks.text: Lava, Intel's open-source framework, describes networks as communicating processes that can run on a CPU for development and then on Loihi. Nengo also had a Loihi backend (nengo-loihi), so NEF models compile to the chip.

Published comparisons (Davies et al. 2021) found the largest energy and latency gains over CPUs and GPUs on workloads that are sparse, recurrent or need online adaptation: constraint satisfaction, nearest-neighbor search, optimization, and small-batch inference with event-camera data. For feedforward deep networks converted to spikes, gains were smaller or absent.

For a cortical column: Loihi is the most natural hardware target for a Thousand Brains-style column, for three reasons. Multi-compartment neurons map onto dendritic segments, on-chip plasticity with traces supports STDP and three-factor rules, and core-local memory suits columns that connect densely inside and sparsely between. Keep fan-in per neuron and synaptic precision modest (weights are low-precision integers) and simulate in Lava on a CPU first.
